item.title: Breaking out: AI Breakouts And The Race Without Brakes
item.description:
OpenAI's models went hacking on their own...
Good day to you. Scientists in Poland have enlisted 2,000 volunteers to help restore the skeleton of a Mastodonsaurus, a 20-foot-long aquatic predator that lived about 240 million years ago. Clean all the bones of terrifying dinosaur era creatures you want, just don’t mix its DNA with a frog’s and open a theme park—that never ends well.

item.title: Lettuce lurch: Supply chain whiplash from lettuce to gas
item.description:
The FDA backtracks but still eyes the iceberg...
Just brew it. We, a newsletter named for your favorite morning beverage, are delighted to report that the American Heart Association (AHA) has deemed it safe—and even potentially beneficial—for most adults to drink up to five cups of coffee per day. In addition to keeping you awake at that 9am meeting, the AHA said the ~400 milligrams of caffeine from three to five cups of joe has been linked to a lower risk of heart disease, stroke, and Type 2 diabetes. However, the AHA did not mention what being around a colleague who just downed five cups of coffee does to your blood pressure.

item.title: Upsizing: Million dollar jackets and the housing gridlock
item.description:
The World Cup generated billions in US economic activity...

item.title: Design Brew: How fonts and logos steer your behavior
item.description:
From iconic brands to impossible maps...
Good morning. Put on your French beret and open up Adobe Illustrator, because we’re talking all things design. In today’s special edition, we’ll get into brand redesigns that surprisingly worked, hilariously bad fonts, and a brief history of subway maps. We’ll also argue over quiet luxury and explain why all AI logos look like...that. Call your friend who went to RISD and let them know you’re auditing a course in Design Brew.

item.title: Catching up: China's Kimi K3 undercuts Silicon Valley
item.description:
A Chinese AI model shocked Silicon Valley...
It’s time! If you thought human UFC fighters were tough, you should see the robots coming for their jobs. This week, during a humanoid robot fight night in China, one competitor nearly lost its head, but kept on swinging. Though it ultimately lost the bout (once its decapitation was complete), it was still able to hang its head high. Higher, actually.
